prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor counter scene where a tall upright fixture on the far right is the nearest surface at roughly 0.4–0.6 metres (brightest white), a curly-haired person in an olive jacket stands directly in front of the camera wearer on the left at about 0.7–1.0 metres (light grey), and a long-haired woman in a brown sweater stands behind a counter at center-right about 1.8–2.2 metres away (mid-dark grey), roughly 1.0–1.2 metres beyond the foreground person. Both the right-hand display stand and the foreground person's back and right arm are within arm's reach of the camera wearer, while a red shopping basket on the counter sits at an intermediate depth (about 1.0–1.3 metres) within arm's reach of both people as the foreground person reaches into and lifts it across frames 1 to 5. Across the five frames, the foreground person shifts slightly leftward and closer to the left frame edge while raising their right arm in frame 5, partially occluding the red basket, the counter, and the lower right side of the woman behind it. The depth map makes the clear metric separation between the foreground display stand, the person in front, the counter plane, and the recessed ceiling/hallway background (3–5+ metres, dark grey to black) much easier to read than in RGB alone. However, it is unreliable on glass and reflective panels—treating the transparent glass partition behind the counter as a flat mid-depth wall and losing fine depth detail around the third partially occluded person holding a phone behind the right-side display rack.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates two main people—a large pink mask on the left for the foreground person (~0.7–1.0 metres away, facing away from the camera wearer toward the counter) and a smaller brown mask at center-right for the woman (~1.8–2.2 metres away, facing forward and slightly left toward the foreground person rather than the camera wearer)—along with a mask on the far right for the upright counter fixture (~0.4–0.6 metres away, cropped by the right frame edge). Across the five frames, the pink foreground mask shifts slightly left and its extended right arm overlaps the lower right portion of the brown person mask in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5 as the foreground person reaches toward and lifts the basket within both people's arm's reach. Compared to RGB, the segmentation map sharply delineates the occluding boundary where the foreground person's right forearm and hand cross in front of the woman's waist and hip area. However, the map is unreliable in several ways: it completely misses the red shopping basket, the counter, the background walls, and the third partially occluded person holding a phone behind the right-side rack. It also misclassifies the tall upright fixture on the far right, flickering between 'tv' and 'cell phone' labels across frames 1 to 5 and missing it entirely in frame 1.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects only the skeleton of the woman standing behind the counter at center-right (roughly 1.8–2.2 metres from the camera wearer), showing her torso and facial keypoints facing forward and angled slightly downward and to the left toward the foreground person and counter rather than looking at the camera wearer. Her shoulders, elbows, and wrists remain below chest level with her forearms brought together in front of her torso within arm's reach of the counter and red basket (~1.0–1.2 metres in front of her), while in frames 1, 3, and 5 her right wrist extends slightly to her right (viewer's left) and in frame 4 magenta hand keypoints appear as her hands meet near her chest. This skeletal overlay makes the subtle flexion of her elbows, the symmetry of her torso, and the exact position of her occluded lower hips behind the counter and behind the foreground person's reaching arm much clearer than in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is unreliable for the rest of the scene because it completely fails to detect the foreground person standing at 0.7–1.0 metres on the left (whose back and reaching right arm dominate the view) as well as the third partially occluded person behind the display rack on the far right, and it only captures fine hand keypoints in frame 4.
